To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
speech stimuli which were not differentiated by traditional measures of speech intelligibility can be differentiated by a more sensitive test methodology.

1) the speech intelligibility measures that were used to evaluate the processed speech in the present study were not sensitive enough to distinguish the speech intelligibility differences between the processed speech and the original speech, 2) the speech intelligility measures that were used in the present study are not sensitive enough to evaluate the speech intelligibility of highly intelligible speech.

1) the intelligibility of processed speech can be evaluated with a variety of measures that are sensitive to the type of processing; 2) some of the measures are sensitive to differences in processing that are not evident with other measures; and 3) the measures can be grouped into three categories that reflect the nature of the processing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of speech intelligibility.
developing a better understanding of the nature of speech intelligibility and how to assess it.
the assessment of the quality of speech produced by a speech processing device.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of more sensitive measures is recommended in the evaluation of intelligible processed speech.
the use of the more sensitive tests in addition to the more conventional tests is recommended in evaluation protocols of speech processing.
the present study shows that the intelligibility of highly intelligible speech can be differentiated by the use of more sensitive tests.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
speech intelligibility can be measured in several ways.
the use of a range of speech stimuli and test methodologies in the evaluation of processed speech is recommended.
the intelligibility of speech is not a unitary concept.
The main takeaway from our work is that
speech stimuli that are not differentiated by standard intelligibility tests are differentiated by more sensitive measures of speech intelligibility.
speech intelligibility measures are sensitive to the processing of the speech.
the use of more sensitive measures of intelligibility can help identify subtle differences in the quality of speech.
